% Fixture: shuffled-stream
% Pages whose content-stream order is deliberately NOT the reading order.
% In ordinary LaTeX output the order in which text is drawn (and therefore the
% order of pdf.js text items) usually matches reading order, so an algorithm
% can look correct just by keeping item order. Here every block is placed at
% an absolute position with textpos and the blocks are emitted in a scrambled
% order, so only geometry can recover the reading order.
%
% US Letter. Page 1: two columns under a full-width title and abstract.
% Page 2: one column. Positions are in inches from the top-left corner.
\documentclass[10pt]{article}
\input{fixture-common}
\usepackage[letterpaper,margin=0.75in]{geometry}
\usepackage[absolute]{textpos}
\setlength{\TPHorizModule}{1in}
\setlength{\TPVertModule}{1in}
\pagestyle{empty}
\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}

% Left column x = 0.75in, right column x = 4.45in, width 3.3in each.
\newcommand{\leftcol}[2]{\begin{textblock*}{3.3in}(0.75in,#1in)#2\end{textblock*}}
\newcommand{\rightcol}[2]{\begin{textblock*}{3.3in}(4.45in,#1in)#2\end{textblock*}}
\newcommand{\fullwidth}[2]{\begin{textblock*}{7in}(0.75in,#1in)#2\end{textblock*}}

\begin{document}
\null
% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 1
% Emission order: right-2, left-1, right-1, abstract, left-2, title.
\rightcol{4.2}{%
  In the second paragraph of the right column we note that the drawing order
  inside a file is an accident of the software that wrote it. Two files that
  look identical on screen can store their text in completely different
  orders.}
\leftcol{2.9}{%
  \textbf{1\quad Introduction}\par\medskip
  The first paragraph of the left column is where reading begins below the
  abstract. In this file it is stored after the second paragraph of the right
  column, so a reader that trusts the storage order will start in the wrong
  place.}
\rightcol{2.9}{%
  \textbf{2\quad Storage order}\par\medskip
  The right column opens with a new section. It is read only after both
  paragraphs of the left column, even though it sits at the same height as
  the first of them.}
\fullwidth{1.6}{%
  \centerline{\textbf{Abstract}}\par\smallskip
  This page stores its paragraphs in a scrambled order. The title is drawn
  last, the abstract in the middle, and the columns out of sequence, so the
  order of the extracted text items says nothing about the order in which a
  person reads the page.}
\leftcol{4.2}{%
  The second paragraph of the left column continues the introduction. After
  it the reader moves to the top of the right column, not to the paragraph
  that happens to be stored next.}
\fullwidth{0.9}{%
  \centerline{\Large Reading Order Without Storage Order}}
\clearpage

% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 2
% Emission order: third, first, second.
\null
\fullwidth{4.0}{%
  The third paragraph closes the page. It is stored first of the three, so it
  is the first text item that pdf.js returns for this page.}
\fullwidth{1.0}{%
  \textbf{3\quad A single column}\par\medskip
  The first paragraph on this page sits at the top. Even a single column can
  be stored out of order when a document has been edited by several tools.}
\fullwidth{2.5}{%
  The second paragraph lies between the other two and is stored last. Sorting
  the blocks from top to bottom is enough to read this page correctly.}
\end{document}
